company.snapshot: Homage (homage.com) is a Columbus, OH-based direct-to-consumer apparel brand specializing in vintage and retro-styled licensed merchandise across major sports leagues (NFL, MLB, NBA, WNBA, MLS, NCAA) and pop culture franchises (Star Wars, Marvel, Disney). They sell through a single Shopify Plus storefront and distribute via EDI to licensed-apparel retailers including Fanatics, Dick's Sporting Goods, and Rallyhouse. They operate a meaningful in-house engineering stack on AWS and are executing a competitive iPaaS evaluation to replace Celigo.
company.industry: Retail / e-commerce (licensed sports and pop culture apparel)

phase1.label: Connected
phase1.headline: All 23 Shopify ↔ NetSuite flows live on MuleSoft — orders, inventory, products, customers, fulfillments, returns, and billing flowing in real time
phase1.body: Every order placed on homage.com flows into NetSuite immediately as a cash sale or sales order, with routing logic applied. Inventory levels — including CSWOS tiered thresholds — sync from NetSuite to Shopify in near-real-time. Fulfillments write back automatically. Returns from Loop reconcile to NetSuite without manual intervention. Matrix item updates and Shopify metafields stay in sync. Customer deposit records create themselves when Shopify payments settle. The manual correction cycles that Sikich currently handles disappear. Celigo is fully decommissioned.

phase2.label: Automated
phase2.headline: NetSuite inventory and EDI demand signals drive Shopify merchandising automatically — no manual CSWOS updates, no stockout surprises
phase2.body: With Phase 1 data flowing reliably, business rules enforce themselves. NetSuite inventory drops below a threshold → Shopify automatically applies CSWOS rules for that SKU — no manual toggle. An EDI purchase order arrives from Fanatics or DSG → NetSuite checks available inventory and flags any potential fulfillment risk before the acknowledgment is sent. Matrix item price changes in NetSuite propagate to Shopify within minutes. Month-end financial close shrinks from days to hours as billing transactions, customer deposits, and invoice transformations all run without human touch.

phase3.label: Agentic
phase3.headline: An AI agent monitors every SKU's velocity, EDI demand, and restock lead time — surfacing margin risk 72 hours before a stockout
phase3.body: Your Phase 1 data — order intake, inventory levels, fulfillment events, EDI demand from Fanatics/DSG/Rallyhouse — becomes the input layer for an AI agent that watches each SKU continuously. When sales velocity plus open EDI demand plus restock lead time signal a stockout risk, the agent surfaces it 72 hours in advance and recommends a specific action: apply CSWOS, restrict EDI allocation, request emergency restock, or initiate a markdown. No spreadsheet. No Monday morning surprise. The operational question it answers: 'Which SKUs are at risk of missing a Fanatics or DSG fulfillment window in the next three days, and what exactly should we do about it?'

prerequisites: Token-Based Authentication (TBA) integration role provisioned in NetSuite — Sikich to create
Consumer key + consumer secret + token ID + token secret generated and stored securely
NetSuite Subsidiary confirmed and mapped (required for all record creation)
Custom record types used in UC10 (store-level metadata) already exist in NetSuite
NetSuite integration account (not a named-user account) set up with least-privilege access to Transactions, Inventory, Customers, Products, and Custom Records
If REST API: PS256 JWT Java helper library confirmed available in deployment environment

scopeBoundary.inScope: MuleSoft ↔ NetSuite API connectivity; CRUD on Transactions, Inventory, Customers, Products, Custom Records
scopeBoundary.assumedPreExists: NetSuite instance live and configured; subsidiaries, chart of accounts, tax codes established; custom record types created by Sikich
scopeBoundary.outOfScope: NetSuite SuiteScript development; new custom record type creation; Chart of Accounts changes; Sikich-managed configuration

prerequisites: Custom App created in Shopify Partner Dashboard with required API scopes: read_orders, write_orders, read_inventory, write_inventory, read_products, write_products, read_customers, write_customers, read_fulfillments, write_fulfillments
Webhook subscriptions registered per flow (orders/create, orders/updated, fulfillments/create, products/update) — MuleSoft will manage webhook receipt
Metafield namespaces and keys defined in Shopify Admin before product sync goes live (UC5 depends on this)
Shopify variant ID ↔ NetSuite item ID cross-reference table established (required for UC4 inventory sync)

scopeBoundary.inScope: MuleSoft ↔ Shopify API (REST and/or GraphQL Admin API); webhook ingestion; metafield management per UC5
scopeBoundary.assumedPreExists: Shopify Plus storefront live; product catalog, collections, and metafield definitions set up; Custom App credentialed
scopeBoundary.outOfScope: Shopify theme development; Shopify app development; storefront customization; Shopify Payments configuration

prerequisites: Orderful account active with API credentials (API key) provisioned
Trading partner configurations for Fanatics, DSG, and Rallyhouse already established in the Orderful portal
X12 transaction sets (810, 856, 997) confirmed and mapped per partner in Orderful
Confirm whether MuleSoft connects to Orderful via REST API or direct X12/AS2 — determines connector choice

scopeBoundary.inScope: MuleSoft → Orderful API calls to send/receive EDI documents (if in scope)
scopeBoundary.assumedPreExists: Orderful account live; partner trading relationships established; EDI maps configured in Orderful
scopeBoundary.outOfScope: Orderful account setup; partner EDI mapping; trading partner onboarding

prerequisites: Carrier integrations (EasyPost, Amazon Shipping) already configured in ShipStation
Turbine middleware logic documented before decommission — DataSkate needs the field mapping and business rules before replacing Turbine with a MuleSoft flow

scopeBoundary.inScope: NetSuite → MuleSoft → ShipStation flow (if Turbine replacement is in scope)
scopeBoundary.assumedPreExists: ShipStation account live; carriers configured; existing Turbine logic documented
scopeBoundary.outOfScope: ShipStation account setup; carrier rate negotiation; EasyPost/Amazon Shipping configuration

aiThoughtStarters: Retailers with NetSuite + Shopify data connected are using AI to optimize markdown timing — identifying which licensed SKUs to discount before they hit dead stock, protecting margin automatically before a Fanatics or DSG reorder window closes.

Other apparel brands are using connected EDI + ERP data to build an AI agent that monitors partner fulfillment risk — flagging when a Fanatics PO can't be filled 48 hours in advance, so the team can reallocate or negotiate rather than take a chargeback.

A mid-market ecommerce brand with the same Shopify + NetSuite + ShipStation stack used integrated order data to build an AI agent that selects carrier in real time based on margin, speed, and inventory location — reducing cost per shipped order by 18%.

Ecommerce brands running Shopify + NetSuite are using AI to predict which new licensed products (new franchise launches, NCAA seasons) will spike demand — automatically staging inventory reorders before sell-out events occur.
